 LLM endpoints where service quality can vary invisibly between requests. The work includes
 



 model serving, fine\-tuning workflows, evaluation infrastructure, and making self\-hosted models
 



 actually usable in production.

 community mailing lists, including content ingestion, multi\-stage processing with human approval
 



 gates, and editorial selection workflows. The work involves agent orchestration where appropriate,
 



 but primarily focuses on systems that augment human reviewers rather than replace them.

 long\-running open\-source projects (Mailman 3, Postorius, and others) that need authentication
 



 integration, feature enhancement, and the kind of careful upstream\-compatible modification that

 the rest are tools you have used in production, not just in coursework.

 RAG pipelines, structured generation, evaluation frameworks, prompt engineering. You know the
 



 difference between a working demo and a system that holds up in production, and you understand
 



 when frontier models are the right tool and when they are not.
 



 • LLM infrastructure and serving. You have deployed models — vLLM, Triton, multi\-model
 



 routing, inference optimization, evaluation pipelines. You think about cost\-per\-token, latency tails,
 



 determinism, and how to keep complex serving systems reliable.

 observability, and operational discipline. ETL is in your background, even if the new pipelines have
 



 ML components in them. You think about what happens when stage three fails after stage two has

 work. Some familiarity with — or curiosity about — the open\-source world helps.
